review_notes:
I read the whole file and checked each new concept against the Mathlib counterpart I know of. I ran no searches of the Mathlib, Batteries or core sources, so this rests on my reading of the file and my knowledge of those libraries.

- `Kernel` is a bundled measurable map `α → Measure β`. It has its own `FunLike` instance and uses the generic `IsZeroApply`, `IsAddApply`, `IsSMulApply` and `FunLike.addCommMonoid` machinery. It doesn't compete with an existing bundled concept.
- `Kernel.sum` is the kernel-level analogue of `Measure.sum`. It is defined through `Measure.sum` and `Measure.measurable_of_measurable_coe`, so it is a lifted specialisation, not a duplicate.
- `IsFiniteKernel`, `IsMarkovKernel` and `IsSFiniteKernel` are uniform-in-`a` versions of `IsFiniteMeasure`, `IsProbabilityMeasure` and `SFinite`. They are stronger, as the module docstring explains, and they connect to the measure classes through instances (`IsFiniteKernel.isFiniteMeasure`, `IsSFiniteKernel.sfinite`). That is integration, not a competing version.
- `Kernel.bound` is a `⨆` of total masses. It has no existing Mathlib counterpart that I know of.
- The deprecated aliases already redirect to the generic `FunLike` lemmas, so earlier duplication has been removed.
- `finsetSum_apply'` and `sum_apply'` are theorems, which the rubric excludes. They are also not a separate version of any concept.

Nothing in the file is an independent, avoidable competing version of an existing concept. The remaining uncertainty is that I did not search the Mathlib tree for a hidden bundled "measurable map into Measure" structure.
